protocol.name: wayluck_wm_unstable_v1

description.summary: a window manager placing windows for wayluck

protocol.description:
The contract between wayluck and the window manager. The window manager owns placement: where each window goes, what's shown and what isn't. wayluck owns clients, buffers and pixels, and applies what it's told.
Unstable: changed in place, without version bumps, until it's frozen as wayluck_wm_v1. A window manager and a wayluck from different commits may not understand each other.

interface.name: wayluck_wm_manager_v1

description.summary: the window manager's connection to wayluck

interface.description: Bound by the one window manager. On binding, wayluck sends an output event for every output and a window event for every window, then ready. After that, it sends them as they appear.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: stop managing

request.description: Windows keep their places until another window manager binds.

request.name: transaction

description.summary: start a transaction

request.description: Changes made through it are applied together on commit, or not at all.

description.summary: modifier keys, as X numbers them

request.name: bind_key

description.summary: take a key combination from clients

request.description: While the binding exists, pressing keysym with exactly these modifiers (Caps Lock and Num Lock aside) goes to the window manager as pressed, and not to the focused client. A keysym matches the key as typed and as it is without modifiers, so shift+1 is bound as 1.

request.name: bind_button

description.summary: take a pointer button combination from clients

request.description: Like bind_key, for a mouse button: pressing it with exactly these modifiers goes to the window manager as pressed, and its release as released (whatever the modifiers are by then), not to the client under the pointer.

request.name: grab_pointer

description.summary: keep the pointer from clients

request.description: For a drag the window manager does itself (moving a window, say): until ungrab_pointer, no client sees the pointer move or its buttons. pointer_position keeps coming.

description.summary: give the pointer back to clients

request.name: warp_pointer

description.summary: move the pointer

request.description: To x, y in global coordinates, as if the user had moved it there: clients under it hear, and pointer_position follows. Nested in another session, that session's cursor stays where it is.

request.name: set_keymap

description.summary: the keyboard's layout, by XKB names

request.description: As in setxkbmap: an empty string is XKB's default (layout "us"). Clients get the new keymap, and key bindings match keys as it has them. A keymap XKB can't make is ignored. Wayluck and it's wm run on the same machine, so wayluck compiles the keymap itself and no file descriptor has to cross the protocol.

request.name: set_layout

description.summary: switch to one of the keymap's layouts

request.description: By its place in set_keymap's layout list, from 0.

event.name: unavailable

description.summary: another window manager is bound

event.description: This manager does nothing; the client should destroy it.

description.summary: a new output

event.name: window

description.summary: a new window

event.description:
A toplevel that wants to be shown, announced at its client's first commit: its title, app_id, parent, size_hints and a fullscreen_request, as far as its client set them up, follow at once. Until a transaction places it, it isn't shown.
Its id is wayluck's name for it, in its log too: it stays the same for the window's life and isn't reused.

event.name: usable

description.summary: the part windows may use

event.description: What bars and panels (layer-shell surfaces' exclusive zones) leave of the output, in global coordinates: where windows should go. Sent with geometry, and again when it changes, before done.

description.summary: a toplevel window
forget the window (after closed)
ask the client to close it

event.name: closed

description.summary: the window is gone; destroy it

event.description: It's no longer shown, and placing it does nothing.

event.name: focus_request

description.summary: the user clicked it

event.description: wayluck doesn't focus it: the window manager decides, with a transaction's focus.

description.summary: the pointer is over it now
the pointer isn't over it any more

event.name: fullscreen_request

description.summary: its client asked to be fullscreen

event.description: F11 in a browser, say. Nothing changes unless the window manager makes it so, with a transaction's fullscreen.

description.summary: its client asked to stop being fullscreen

event.name: parent

description.summary: the window it belongs to

event.description: A dialog's main window, say (null: none). Sent with the window, and again when its client changes it.

event.name: size_hints

description.summary: the sizes its client can work with

event.description: Its client's smallest and largest size (0: no limit). The same smallest and largest: a window of one size, like a dialog or a splash screen. Sent with the window, and again when they change.

description.summary: a key combination the window manager has
give it back to clients
the user pressed it
a pointer button combination the window manager has
give it back to clients
the user pressed it
the user let go of the button

interface.name: wayluck_wm_transaction_v1

description.summary: changes applied together

interface.description: Requests made before commit are collected, not applied. After commit, the transaction takes no more requests; wayluck answers with applied or failed, and then it should be destroyed.

description.summary: drop it; uncommitted changes are discarded

request.name: place

description.summary: show a window at a rectangle

request.description: Global coordinates. The client is asked to take that size; whatever size it commits, the window is shown at x, y. Stacking: the windows a transaction places go above every other window, in the order they're placed, the last on top.

description.summary: stop showing a window
apply everything in this transaction, together

request.name: focus

description.summary: give a window the keyboard

request.description: With no window, no window has it. The focused window is drawn as active; where it stacks is up to place.

request.name: border

description.summary: draw a border around a window

request.description: width pixels wide, outside the window's rectangle (place gives the rectangle inside it); 0 draws none. Colours are 0xAARRGGBB, one for each side. A window has no border until it's given one.

request.name: tiled

description.summary: say which edges of a window are tiled

request.description: The edges that meet other windows or the output's: the client is told (xdg_toplevel's tiled states), and draws for it, e.g. without shadows, and without rounding its size to whole character cells. A window has none until it's given some.

request.name: fullscreen

description.summary: tell a window whether it's fullscreen

request.description: The client is told (xdg_toplevel's fullscreen state) and draws for it, without its own chrome. Where it goes, and how big, is still up to place. A window isn't fullscreen until it's told so.

description.summary: the changes are on screen

event.name: failed

description.summary: nothing was applied

event.description: For example, a window in it was closed first.
